newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Yukong keeps reformer No.1 shut, restarts No.2.
newsitem.headline: Yukong keeps reformer No.1 shut, restarts No.2.

text.p: South Korea's largest refiner Yukong Ltd has extended the shutdown of its 8,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) reformer No.1 until the end of February but restarted its 15,000-bpd No.2 unit from February 1, an industry source said on Wednesday.
Both units which process naphtha into reformate, a gasoline component, were shutdown on Janaury 24 due to bad margins.
"The reformate price compared to naphtha is not so good, so it is better to shutdown," the source said, explaining Yukong's decision to extend the shutdown of one unit.

The source also said the decison was partly due to a fall in Yukong's total reformate demand by two million barrels per year (5,500-bpd) as South Korea reduced its gasoline octane requirement from 95-octane to 93-octane on February 1.
"Yukong does not need that much reformate now," the source said.
The decison to restart the first unit will made at the end of February and will depend on the gasoline price in the Korean domestic market, the source said.

Gasoline prices are expected to increase in the coming months as the summer driving season approaches, and there was a "more than 50 percent" likelihood that the unit will be restarted in early March, he said.
